nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture from power plants_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does the production of greenhouse gas emissions in Sri Lanka differ from the U.S.?
nodes.answer: The production of greenhouse gas emissions in Sri Lanka did not consider building energy use, which underestimates the environmental impact of production compared to the U.S.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture from power plants_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How are consumption-based CO2 emissions different from production-based emissions?
nodes.answer: Consumption-based CO2 emissions consider the emissions traded with goods in addition to production-based emissions, providing a more comprehensive view of a country's total emissions impact.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture from power plants_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the effect of the scrubber on particle number concentrations at the 20 kW and 60 kW loads?
nodes.answer: The particle number concentrations were reduced by 25% at the 20 kW load and by 38% at the 60 kW load after passing through the scrubber.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture from power plants_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Which greenhouse gas emissions does the analysis primarily focus on and why?
nodes.answer: The analysis primarily focuses on carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions because they account for the largest share of GHG emissions and are largely by-products of energy consumption.
